title: VW’s Scania hastens China e-truck push as drivers abandon diesel
article:
(Oct 20): Volkswagen AG’s truck unit Scania AB is speeding up plans to make electric trucks at its new Chinese factory as record diesel prices fuel a faster-than-expected switch in the world’s biggest market.

The Swedish truckmaker will manufacture battery-powered vehicles at its plant in Rugao, China, as soon as it receives a licence, chief executive officer Christian Levin said in an interview in Södertälje. Levin expects electric trucks to account for half of China’s market by the start of 2027.

“We have had to speed up those plans,” Levin said. “It’s always quite a complicated process in China to get licences to do different things, but I have to say: it has moved much faster than we could have imagined.”

Chinese electric-truck sales jumped almost 80% in the first half from a year earlier, according to BloombergNEF, and are on pace to account for close to a third of all trucks sold this year. That compares with just 8% a couple of years ago.

E-truck demand is getting a boost from trade-in subsidies and elevated diesel prices in the wake of the US-Iran war. Beijing had targeted a 40% market share for such vehicles by 2030, with the current trajectory outpacing this goal. As part of the switch to battery power, China’s consumption of diesel is projected to fall more than 10% this year, according to the Sinopec Economics & Development Research Institute.

See also: EU officials propose guardrails for insurance risk transfer boom

Scania, which is part of Traton SE, opened the Rugao plant last year, its first wholly-owned factory in China alongside production in Europe and Latin America. The facility, which serves China and other Asian markets, can make both conventional and battery-powered trucks.

“It is happening quickly and that’s incredibly fascinating,” Levin said. “It means they have found a way to expand charging infrastructure and the power grid, which is the biggest challenge we have in many countries around the world, including Europe.”

Electric big rigs taking off in China will likely ratchet up competitive pressure on Traton, Daimler Truck Holding AG and Volvo AB. German supplier ZF Friedrichshafen AG last month said the “centre of gravity for electric-drive technology” in trucks was in China.

See also: Legacy carmakers seen losing mass market to Chinese rivals

As China’s market pivots, the US is lagging after electrification incentives were cut. Levin said high diesel prices are likely to move the needle now.

“If diesel prices continue to rise, then purely on its own merits, it will become cheaper to drive on electricity even in the US,” he said.

Traton’s conventional truck business has remained resilient despite the burden from record diesel prices, which typically slows investment in new vehicles. Traton’s US-based truck arm posted a 48% jump in third-quarter vehicle sales, helping drive a 10% increase for the group.

“It’s been very much about customers looking for energy-efficient solutions,” he said. Customers are also willing to pay more for fuel efficiency, he added.

In Europe, the backdrop for e-trucks remains tough. Poor charging infrastructure and grid capacity are combining with high operating costs, Levin said. The prevalence of small haulage companies means changes in customers can cancel routes e-trucks can serve.

“Then you’re left with a stranded asset,” Levin said. The average European haulage company operates just seven or eight trucks.

Levin spoke as Scania inaugurated a new 975 million-krona vehicle testing facility in Södertälje, south of Stockholm. The 850,000-square-metre site includes a high-speed oval and areas for testing vehicle handling, rollover safety and autonomous driving.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Levin said driverless trucks could be used at scale in the US before 2030, while Europe may take longer because of regulatory hurdles, particularly for vehicles crossing national borders.

Traton is due to report third-quarter earnings on Oct 28.

title: Wee Hur secures unconditional option to acquire Sydney site for 471-bed PBSA
article:
Wee Hur Holdings has secured an unconditional option to acquire a site at 35-51 Nicholson Street in Wollstonecraft, Sydney for an undisclosed amount.

The 2,744 sq m (29,536.17 sq ft) freehold site is earmarked for a 12-storey purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) that can house 471 beds. The PBSA, which is located about a three-minute walk from Crows Nest Metro Station, will offer a mix of studio, ensuite rooms and two-bedroom apartments, along with communal indoor and outdoor living spaces and amenities.

Sited within the Crows Nest Transport Oriented Development (Tod) Accelerated Precinct, one of eight precincts identified by the New South Wales Government for accelerated rezoning around major transport hubs, the future PBSA is also within walking distance of amenities, supermarkets and dining options.

The location is connected to several universities, including the University of Sydney, the University of Technology Sydney and Macquarie University.

The proposed acquisition and development will be done via a special purpose vehicle (SPV) with external capital partners, says Wee Hur. The group will retain an equity interest that is subject to the finalisation of the investment structure.

Intergen Property Group, a boutique property investment management group in Sydney will serve as the local investment manager for the project. The development will be undertaken by Wee Hur Capital.

See also: Wee Hur enters Singapore student housing market with 1,398-bed property at NTU

The proposed acquisition is expected to be completed around 2H2027, subject to the exercise of the option and completion of the transaction in accordance with its terms.

Upon completion, the PBSA will operate under Wee Hur’s Y Suites student accommodation brand. The group currently operates two PBSAs under the brand - the 409-bed Y Suites on Margaret at Regent Street in Sydney and the 708-bed Y Suites on Frome at 188 Grenfell Street in Adelaide. Y Suites on Frome is targeted to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2027.

“We remain cautiously optimistic about the Australian student accommodation market, particularly as we observe evolving government policies and demand sentiment from key international student markets,” says Goh Wee Ping, CEO of Wee Hur Capital and CIO of Wee Hur Holdings. “Therefore, we are also increasingly selective about where we invest. Nicholson is a good example of what we look for – a well-connected location, convenient access to major universities and an established neighbourhood with the amenities that students value.”

See also: Centurion expands PBSA footprint with Adelaide, Hong Kong acquisitions totalling $82 mil

“By combining these fundamentals with our development and operating capabilities, alongside capital partners, we believe we can continue growing our PBSA platform while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation,” he adds.

Shares in Wee Hur closed 1 cent higher or 1.71% up at 59.5 cents on Oct 20.

title: GCash owner erases gains in debut after record Philippines IPO
article:
(Oct 20): Mynt Inc, the operator of the mobile-payments app GCash, gained in its debut on Tuesday after the biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO) in the Philippines.

The shares rose as much as 2.1% to 6.74 pesos in early trading. Mynt sold 8.03 billion shares at 6.60 pesos apiece to raise about 53 billion pesos (US$840 million or $1.07 billion), topping noodle maker Monde Nissin Corp’s offering in 2021.

The fintech firm’s IPO, a rare play on the country’s expanding digital economy, drew cornerstone commitments from more than 20 investors, including BlackRock Inc, FIL Investment Management and Schroders. It values Mynt at about 442 billion pesos, which would make it the third-largest listed financial firm in the Philippines and the seventh-largest overall, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

The enthusiasm surrounding the deal has raised some hopes for the broader market, which has been dominated by banks, property developers and conglomerates. Market watchers are keen to see whether a new-economy stock can help win back global funds, which are on track to sell Philippine equities for a ninth straight year.

“GCash would broaden the Philippine market, particularly given the shortage of genuine growth stocks,” said Gary Tan, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments in Singapore.

See also: Singapore's Sea starts enterprise cloud foray while eyeing fintech arm IPO

Philippine stocks have struggled over the past decade due to structural challenges like limited market diversity and sluggish turnover. The country’s weight in MSCI Inc’s global emerging-markets index has shrunk to almost nothing while the MSCI Philippines Index has just nine members, with one port operator accounting for almost 45% of the benchmark.

The energy shock unleashed by the Middle East war has also weighed on local assets this year. The Philippine Stock Exchange Index slumped to an 11-month low earlier in October while the peso has hit a record low. Foreign investors have sold about US$623 million of local shares in 2026.

See also: JPMorgan and Alibaba are said among investors in Dongshan’s listing — Bloomberg

Despite the underperformance, valuations offer little comfort for long-term investors. The MSCI Philippines gauge trades at about 9.5 times its one-year forward earnings, versus a multiple of nine times for the broader emerging-market gauge, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

A combination of a growing financial-services platform and demand from international institutions gives Mynt’s offering a profile that is largely missing from Manila’s traditional equity benchmarks. Its GCash platform serves tens of millions of users, giving investors access to a business tied to digital payments, consumer lending and financial services.

The company plans to use the proceeds from the share sale to expand its digital financial services, develop new products, and for general corporate purposes.

“The GCash IPO is a positive development for the Philippine equity market as it puts the country back on the radar of international investors, particularly those looking for exposure to fintech and digital financial services,” said Ron Acoba, the chief investment strategist of Trading Edge Consultancy in Manila.

title: Asia refiners in dispute with Saudis over 2027 oil contracts
article:
(Oct 20): Saudi Aramco’s term-contract negotiations with Asian oil refiners have run into trouble due to disagreements over outstanding purchases in existing deals, said traders involved in the discussions.

The disputes are a byproduct of the Middle East war, which cut exports from the region and meant that Saudi Arabia’s customers weren’t able to collect their contracted supply. That forced refiners to switch to a more opportunistic mode of buying Persian Gulf oil via the spot market.

To satisfy this demand, Aramco ramped up spot sales to Asia from early September, taking advantage of a recovery in flows through the Strait of Hormuz even as attacks on ships continued.

The world’s No 1 crude exporter is now trying to revert to selling more oil under contract for next year. The crux of the argument is whether the recent wave of spot-market purchases can count towards refiners’ annual contractual obligations this year, according to the traders, asking not to be named as they’re not authorised to speak to the media.

If spot buying is excluded many Asian refiners won’t be able to meet their 2026 contracts with Aramco, the traders said. Some processors are arguing the prompt buying should be included in their contractual obligations, but Aramco is pushing back and saying they must take more oil under contract next year to make up for the shortfall, they said.

See also: Asian LNG prices jump to highest since 2022 on tanker strikes

At least one refiner has been asked by Aramco to compensate for this year’s shortfall by committing to taking more crude in 2027, something which it’s balking at, the traders said.

Many Asian oil buyers are reticent to commit to more contracted purchases next year, given the uncertainties over flows as the war shows little sign of ending. The dispute is spilling over into the spot market and slowing down purchases of Saudi crude, as well as oil from other Middle Eastern producers.

See also: Qatar LNG cargo makes rare Red Sea journey to get gas to Europe

Term-contract discussions for the coming year normally conclude by the end of October, as Asian refiners typically order January-loading Middle Eastern crude from the spot market in November, and need to know how much oil they will be taking under term contracts next year before they can make those buying decisions.

Similar negotiations with other Persian Gulf producers are also going on at the moment. Abu Dhabi National Oil Co, the United Arab Emirates’ biggest oil company, is allowing spot crude purchases to count towards some Asian refiners’ annual oil-import obligations this year, although no decision has been reached on whether this arrangement will continue into 2027.

“As a resilient and reliable energy provider, Adnoc remains committed to supporting our customers across Asia and providing flexibility as we meet their requirements,” the company said in a response to questions.

The question of how Asian refiners will buy oil from the Middle East will remain uncertain until the security situation in the region stabilises. Aramco has floated the idea of changing pricing benchmarks and delivery terms in its supply contracts. One option under consideration is that the Saudi producer will take on the responsibility of transporting the crude directly to some of its Asian customers.

title: SIAS CEO welcomes rising corporate governance standards but notes gap between large and small companies
article:
Singapore’s corporate governance standards have gone up over the past year, but the gap between large-cap and small-cap companies continues to persist, says David Gerald, the founder, president and CEO of the Securities Investors Association (Singapore) (SIAS).

Gerald was speaking at the launch of the SIAS Corporate Governance Week at Orchard Hotel Singapore on Oct 20 when he touched on the research that was conducted by the Centre for Governance and Sustainability at the National University of Singapore (NUS) Business School for the SIAS’s 2026 Singapore Corporate Governance Award.

NUS’s study, which covered 458 publicly listed companies, found that the average corporate governance score had risen to 66% in 2026 from 65.6% in 2025. Large-cap companies fared the best, with an average score of 73.2%. This was followed by mid-cap companies with an average score of 68.1% and small-cap companies at 64.3%.

“An improvement is welcome, but we should interpret it carefully. The increase was modest and was partly influenced by a shift in the sample towards larger companies, which generally achieve higher scores,” Gerald says.

“The message is therefore not that Singapore has solved corporate governance,” Gerald adds. “It is that progress continues, but slowly, and that the gap between larger and smaller companies remains clear. Smaller listed companies form the majority of the market and cannot be left behind. Proportionate governance may recognise differences in scale and resources, but proportionate must never mean second-rate.”

In his remarks, Gerald made reference to the proliferation of AI tools in the workplace and cautioned investors and board members from letting AI substitute human judgment when making decisions. “As AI becomes embedded in operations, boards must know who owns the risk, how it is monitored and when a human being must intervene,” Gerald says.

See also: ECB’s Sleijpen says window is closing to limit warming impact

“The same warning applies to investors. AI can help screen companies, compare valuations and summarise annual reports. It cannot abolish investment risk. Investors must still understand what they are buying, assess the business model and balance sheet, judge management’s credibility and decide whether the price is reasonable.”

title: Ryanair CEO predicts historic jump in air fares next year
article:
(Oct 20): Ryanair Holdings plc chief executive officer Michael O’Leary predicted a record increase in European air fares next year as the Middle East war continues to drive up oil prices, forcing airlines to pass on their fuel costs to consumers.

Ticket prices are set to increase by as much as 20% next year, O’Leary said on Tuesday during a press conference in Brussels. As a result, airline margins will get squeezed because even the jump in fuel surcharges won’t make up for the higher oil bill, he said.

“You’re going to see the biggest increase in airfares, I would say, in history in Europe in the next 12 months,” O’Leary said. “The question is, will that increase in airfares be enough to cover the dramatically higher oil bills? I don’t think it will be.”

The comments by the head of Europe’s largest budget carrier add to the more pessimistic outlook for the aviation industry, which has been forced to contend with a dramatic jump in costs even as travellers continue to splurge on air tickets.

O’Leary said most European airlines, including his own, lack significant hedging next year to protect against higher oil prices. In addition, there’s less capacity in the market as some airlines struggle, while higher taxes are further dimming the picture for the industry.

“We are 85% unhedged next year, and most of the other European airlines are in a similar position,” he said.

See also: Legacy airline stocks favoured over low-cost carriers as fuel prices stay high

Ryanair dropped as much as 2.1%, bringing the decline to 25% for the year. At that rate, that would be the worst annual stock return since 2018.

The CEO used his expletive-laden press conference to dish out against regulation in markets like France and Belgium, where Ryanair will reduce its footprint in response to higher taxes. He reiterated that the European aviation industry will continue to consolidate as weaker players struggle to survive in a high-cost environment.

Air Baltic Corp and Spain’s Volotea are the latest European carriers to undergo restructuring as higher costs take their toll. Last week, Deutsche Lufthansa AG won the race against Air France-KLM to acquire a stake in Portugal’s state-owned TAP. Meanwhile, US private equity firm Apollo Global Management Inc is laying out the framework to take over EasyJet plc.

See also: Thailand eyes US$30 departure tax for tourists in revenue push

Airlines across the world have suffered from soaring jet fuel costs since the Iran war began in late February. Ryanair’s most recent earnings in July showed the conflict hit its profit and caused later bookings amid concern about jet-fuel supply availability.

O’Leary said separately that he aims to receive the first delivery of the carrier’s Boeing Max 10 aircraft in January, with about 16 more expected through April.

title: AI fears return with data centre firm Elice’s 33% debut flop in Seoul
article:
(Oct 20): Shares of data-centre infrastructure company Elice Inc plunged in their trading debut on Tuesday, underscoring lingering concerns about whether the artificial intelligence (AI) boom can justify the billions of dollars being poured into the industry.

The Seoul-based neocloud service provider’s shares fell sharply from the open and plunged as much as 38%, before finishing the day with a 32% loss. That was the worst-ever opening day for a sizeable South Korean initial public offering (IPO), according to data compiled by Bloomberg. It represented an abrupt downturn after the company raised 201 billion won (US$151 million or $194 million) in an IPO priced at the top of the marketed range, with the retail tranche 400 times subscribed.

The sell-off threatened a tentative recovery in Asian stocks and revived concerns over neoclouds, as rising borrowing costs and doubts over returns from massive AI spending sour investor appetite. CoreWeave Inc’s shares have more than halved since their May peak and its bonds plunged last week, while Australia’s Firmus Grid Ltd scrapped a planned IPO over valuation concerns. Data-centre operator AirTrunk is delaying a planned listing, while Nscale Ltd is facing pushback over its target IPO valuation, Bloomberg News has reported.

“Elice’s debut comes at a time when sentiment towards AI infrastructure companies has weakened, particularly in the US,” said Albert Yong, a managing partner and the chief investment officer of Petra Capital Management. “Sentiment towards AI infrastructure has been highly volatile and often disconnected from underlying fundamentals.”

Founded in 2015 by three students in the doctorate programme of KAIST, one of the country’s top technology universities, Elice began as a coding education platform before pivoting to AI cloud infrastructure, supplying products including servers, liquid-cooled chips, cloud and networking equipment and software. The company has since developed a modular data centre platform with high-density power systems and advanced liquid cooling designed for high-performance AI chip clusters.

Elice sold its shares in the IPO at 90,500 won apiece, for a post-listing market capitalisation exceeding one trillion won. The shares sank to as low as 58,000 won on Tuesday on the tech-heavy Kosdaq market, before rebounding slightly to close at 61,500 won. Mirae Asset Securities Co and Samsung Securities Co served as lead underwriters.

See also: Nscale, Anthropic in talks for US$45 bil cloud computing deal — Bloomberg

The pressure on investor sentiment is against the backdrop of South Korea also weighing tighter scrutiny of new listings. Authorities are examining whether a proposed US IPO of SK Hynix Inc’s unit Solidigm would constitute a “duplicate listing”, a structure in which a company already own by a plublicly traded parent lists its shares separately. Critics argue that such deals can disavantage existing shareholders by allowing a subsidiary’s value to be unlocked separately. The debate adds another layer of uncertainty for companies seeking to tap public markets.

Elice was able to generate demand among South Korean retail investors, who poured roughly 10.3 trillion won into subscription deposits in hopes of buying shares.

See also: AEM’s Kabbani stresses company’s tech chops to ride on AI-driven semi-con wave

The stock’s plunge sent shockwaves across South Korea’s retail investment community, known as ants. On Toss Securities’ popular mobile app, one poster shared an illustration of Alice — spelled similar to Elice in Korean — in Wonderland, smashing ants with a large hammer. “All ants are dying,” the post said above the illustration.

A user on X posted a screenshot of a 68,255 won position, down 24.75%, on the day, saying: “This is the first time I have lost money on an IPO.” Another investor wrote that the stock “ruined South Korean stocks and crypto”, to which a comment said “I just want Elice to go away to Wonderland”.

“Retail investors may have blindly believed that IPO stocks would always go up,” said Jo Hyunik, an investment division manager at Seoul-based Iroom Investment Advisors.

To win over investors, Elice touted a 200% surge in first-half revenue to 34.4 billion won, according to its prospectus. The company swung to an operating profit of 10.3 billion won, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation jumped more than 11-fold to 23.2 billion won. The company is expected to record an 83% sales jump in 2026 and an operating margin of about 33%, analyst Douglas Kim wrote in a note on Smartkarma.

Elice’s financial structure is different from CoreWeave’s, and investors don’t need to view the company as “particularly risky”, said Kim Dojoon, the chief executive officer of Zian Investment Management. But, he added, “It remains to be seen whether the company can maintain its current profitability.”

A successful offering could have helped break an IPO drought in South Korea, where the primary market has been in the doldrums as fundraising surged across Asia. First-time listings in Seoul have raised US$1.4 billion in 2026, compared with more than US$3 billion in each of the previous three years, according to Bloomberg-compiled data. Meanwhile, SK Hynix Inc completed the biggest-ever US share sale by a foreign company.

Elice’s IPO was the biggest on the Kosdaq this year and surpassed in South Korea only by the US$337 million offering of K Bank Co in March.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Backed by venture capital firms including Vertex Ventures and Altos Ventures, Elice plans to use its IPO proceeds to build more AI data centres around South Korea and abroad, according to CEO Jae Won Kim.

“We are going all-in on becoming a full-stack AI infrastructure leader globally,” Kim said in an interview. “This IPO is about giving ourselves the financial firepower to execute.”

title: Maersk and Hateco plan US$3.5 bil Vietnam rail freight project
article:
(Oct 20): AP Moller-Maersk A/S, the world’s No 2 container carrier, signed an agreement with Vietnamese conglomerate Hateco to develop a US$3.5 billion ($4.5 billion) railway container terminal network in northern Vietnam during President To Lam’s official visit to Denmark.

APM Terminals, the port operating unit of AP Moller-Maersk, inked a memorandum of understanding with Hateco in Copenhagen on Tuesday to develop a plan for a rail freight terminal, including cargo handling centres, in the port city of Haiphong, according to a statement from Hateco. The proposed network, which will include three other rail freight facilities in northern provinces, “aims to connect industrial parks, logistics hubs and production zones with major transport hubs”, it said.

The project comes as Vietnam ramps up infrastructure investment to support its multi-year double-digit economic growth target, seeking to boost spending to attract private capital and spur development. The Southeast Asian nation is pouring billions of dollars into upgrading its transport and logistics networks, with railways seen as a key priority.

Maersk has partnered with Hateco on a US$400 million container port project in Haiphong while the two companies are also working on an inland terminal in Hanoi with investment of about US$98 million, according to the Vietnamese company. The Danish shipping giant is also expanding its investment in some joint projects, including the US$2 billion Lien Chieu container terminal port in Danang.

The planned rail freight facilities, which will use digital technology to enhance cargo handling and storage while connecting to seaports and rail infrastructure, are expected to ease road congestion and expand options for cross-border shipments, according to the statement.

title: Panasonic speeds up efforts to turn windows into solar panels
article:
(Oct 20): Panasonic Holdings Corp is accelerating plans to mass-produce solar cells that can be embedded in glass, bolstering Japan’s push into the next-generation technology and expanding renewable energy deployment.

Large-scale production of glass-based perovskite solar cells will begin in April 2029 — a year earlier than previously planned — at a facility in Nagahama, Shiga prefecture, the company said in a statement on Tuesday. Panasonic started selling units made at its development site in Osaka in September.

Japan is betting on thin and lightweight perovskite cells that can be installed on surfaces unsuitable for conventional solar panels, helping the mountainous and densely populated country add more renewables. Panasonic is targeting windows and exterior walls with “power-generating glass” that can be customised in size, transparency and design.

“Particularly in urban areas, many buildings have limited roof space available for solar panel installation, leading to increased expectations for building-integrated photovoltaics,” Panasonic said in the statement, without stating how many units it aimed to produce at the new plant.

Japan is attempting to carve out a share of the emerging market, putting it in competition with China, which dominates the global solar industry and is also developing perovskite technology. The cells are also more expensive than conventional solar panels, a key hurdle to widespread deployment.

title: PBOC faces multi-month road to new rate anchor, analysts say
article:
(Oct 20): China’s central bank may be embarking on a multi-month transition towards an overnight policy interest rate, a shift that will require more frequent liquidity operations using the new benchmark candidate to test market reception, analysts say.

Analysts at Société Générale SA and Tianfeng Securities see the switch as a gradual process rather than a one-off change, following People’s Bank of China governor Pan Gongsheng’s signal that the central bank will study replacing its seven-day benchmark with an overnight tenor.

The transition underscores the central bank’s ongoing efforts to refine its monetary policy framework and to place greater emphasis on interest-rate guidance. How the switch is implemented could directly impact funding costs, which have already helped pull benchmark bond yields towards their lowest close since early 2025.

“The PBOC should be conducting more frequent one-day open market operations and observe whether the transmission is working well to influence short-term rates and reduce volatility,” said Michelle Lam, greater China economist at Société Générale.

“It could take place over the coming months as soon as the fourth quarter. The window is the upcoming quarterly PBOC meeting,” she said.

See also: China's overnight rate set to become main policy benchmark

Demonstrating that step-by-step approach, the PBOC announced it will conduct overnight reverse repos from Oct 21 to Nov 2, moving beyond its prior practice of using such operations strictly during month-end or tax-payment seasons.

Gao Xiang, head of the financial derivatives team at Nanhua Futures Research Institute, said the PBOC’s announcement on overnight reverse repo operations in October and November is intended to lay the groundwork for the transition.

“We believe further groundwork may be needed before the transition to an overnight policy rate can be completed, including increasing the frequency of overnight operations and improving pricing transparency,” he said.

See also: China’s growth rebound tops forecasts to close in on target

While near-term policy meetings may provide further clarity on the framework, a formal switch could take longer to materialise as the central bank tests transmission.

“We expect the overnight open market operation rate may be formally established as the benchmark anchor in the first half of 2027,” Tianfeng Securities analysts led by Liu Jie wrote in a note.

title: Copper mines need US$332 bil new investment to ease shortfall
article:
(Oct 20): Copper mines need about US$332 billion of new investment to avert a future supply shock, according to Bloomberg New Energy Finance (BNEF) estimates.

Without significant capital outlays, the copper market faces a projected supply shortfall of 20 million metric tons by 2050, and is at risk of a painful squeeze that will slow the shift toward electrification, according to a report released Tuesday.

The market is expected to slip into deficit by 2028 as demand rises and producers struggle to replace declining output, BNEF analysts said.

The shift away from fossil fuels and toward electrifying everything from cars to data centres has made copper by far the most supply-constrained metal covered in BloombergNEF’s Transition Metals Outlook report. Demand linked to electrification is projected to spike 89% to 23.3 million tons in 2050, accounting for more than half of total copper consumption.

“Electrified transport is the fastest-growing copper application,” the analysts wrote. “Electric cars, trucks and buses, whose adoption skyrockets over 2026-2050, require copper in motors, inverters, battery packs, high-voltage wiring and charging.”

See also: China buys more US soybeans as purchasing spree gathers pace — Bloomberg

The red metal will also continue to be in demand for construction, industrial production and consumer products, while data centres are just “a drop in the ocean for copper demand”.

Enough copper may exist underground, but new and expanded mines are not coming online fast enough to offset declining output from existing operations. Without additional investment, total supply could fall 14.5% to 25.7 million tons by 2050, from 30 million tons in 2026. Falling ore grades will raise production costs, while recycling won’t be enough to offset lower primary output.

Even if the required US$332 billion is invested in new mines, the gap is likely to remain open until at least 2043 because a new copper mine takes an average of 17 years to develop.

See also: Copper climbs to three-week high on strike threat, Fed comments

Chile is expected to remain the largest primary producer, although its output is forecast to fall to 4.8 million tons in 2050, from 5.8 million tons in 2026, BNEF estimates. The nation’s share of mined supply would nevertheless rise to 28% from 24% as production declines more rapidly elsewhere.

title: SoftBank credit risk hits four-year high on AI funding strain
article:
(Oct 20): SoftBank Group Corp’s credit risk, as measured by its credit-default swaps, has risen to the highest level in nearly four years as concerns grow over artificial intelligence (AI)-related funding and a potential large acquisition.

SoftBank’s five-year CDS stood at 432 basis points on Tuesday, a level unseen since early November 2022, data compiled by Bloomberg show. It has widened by more than 30 basis points since moving above 400 a week earlier.

Concerns over debt-fuelled AI investment have intensified as financial strains at US cloud computing services provider CoreWeave Inc put a spotlight on the sector’s mounting borrowing. SoftBank is also drawing scrutiny as financing costs rise and it weighs an acquisition of Allied Universal.

The last time SoftBank’s CDS was at this level in 2022, its Vision Fund business was posting heavy losses and the group was in defensive mode. Masayoshi Son, who described himself as “an aggressive person”, stepped back from earnings briefings as the company retrenched.

SoftBank’s CDS is the highest among major Japanese companies, exceeding second-ranked Nissan Motor Co’s spread by more than 130 basis points.

See also: Australia to sue Facebook, TikTok for alleged breaches of ban

Bloomberg Intelligence credit analyst Sharon Chen sees at least US$6 billion ($7.7 billion) of cash outflow from SoftBank in the year ending March 2027, with further AI investment adding to funding needs. SoftBank “would need to raise fresh funds for the deal”, while its loan-to-value ratio could move toward its self-imposed 25% ceiling, she said in a note.

SoftBank Group shares have performed poorly of late, falling about 50% from a June high.

title: India steps up overseas investment checks as rupee slides
article:
(Oct 20): India’s central bank is reportedly tightening scrutiny of large overseas investments by domestic companies, as it seeks to contain capital outflows amid pressure on the rupee.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued a standardised checklist to major banks last week, requiring detailed information on overseas direct investments exceeding US$1 billion and transactions above the regulatory limit of four times an investing company’s net worth, the Economic Times reported on Tuesday, citing two unidentified people familiar with the matter.

The initiative comes as the RBI steps up efforts to defend the local currency, which has tumbled more than 5% this year amid persistent dollar demand and capital outflows. The central bank has already tightened rules on corporate currency hedging and sought to curb dollar purchases by importers. Closer scrutiny of overseas investments adds to those efforts, though the RBI hasn’t imposed new restrictions on such investments.

Capital flows out of India have accelerated in recent years, as businesses diversify their supply chains and expand international operations, while Indians also invest in foreign equity markets and startups.

Overseas direct investment (ODI) climbed to US$26.7 billion in the fiscal year that ended in March, almost double the figure of two years earlier, according to data released by the RBI. This year’s numbers point to a further acceleration, with outflows of some US$22.7 billion in the five months through August. ODI investments include equity and debt investments, as well as corporate guarantees issued by local entities.

The largest transaction this year was IT firm Coforge Ltd’s acquisition of Silicon Valley-based artificial intelligence and digital engineering firm Encora, at an enterprise value of US$2.35 billion.

See also: ABB orders surge past expectations as data centres fuel 40% jump

The RBI caps foreign transactions for Indian nationals at US$250,000 per person per year. Wealthy Indians use ODI as an alternative route to make investments abroad, through holding companies or foreign subsidiaries.

The regulator’s threshold for classifying a transaction as ODI includes whether it involves control of the foreign entity or more than 10% of the paid-up equity. Investments by individuals are subject to the same criteria.

Under the RBI’s checklist, banks must independently assess overseas asset valuations, including acquisition premiums and share-swap ratios, rather than simply rely on valuation reports, the Economic Times reported. They must also examine the investing company’s earnings quality, past overseas investments, existing commitments, and ability to withstand financial shocks, the newspaper reported.

See also: Japan’s 20-year bond sale sees strongest demand on record

The RBI did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Bloomberg.

title: ABB orders surge past expectations as data centres fuel 40% jump
article:
(Oct 20): ABB Ltd reported third-quarter orders that surpassed expectations after demand for data centre and utilities electrification components surged.

Comparable orders in the third quarter jumped 40% to $12.1 billion, the Swiss manufacturer said Tuesday. That beat an average analyst estimates of US$11.4 billion.

Separately, the company is pushing on with acquisitions, setting up a joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric Corp for a low-voltage power distribution business in Japan. ABB will pay around US$495 million for a 51% stake in the unit.

The factory automation firm has been profiting from rising investments in data centres needed to feed a surge in artificial intelligence applications. ABB makes the transformers that enable power grids to supply the centres’ substantial energy needs.

Orders in that unit were the third quarter’s key growth engine, accounting for 70% of new business. The motion business grew by 14% while automation was stable.

ABB also made a small upward tweak to its revenue forecast and now sees comparable revenue growth in the ”low teens” range. Previously it said revenue might rise in the low double-digit to low teens range.

See also: Japan’s 20-year bond sale sees strongest demand on record

Year to date, shares have gained around 26% through to Monday’s close. Still, given its exposure to the artificial intelligence industry and build-out, ABB has been caught in the recent faltering global AI trade that’s weighed on markets. Since the start of the month, the stock has declined 7%.

Earlier this year ABB bought British industrial components company Rotork Plc for an enterprise value of around US$5.5 billion to expand its electrification and automation businesses, its biggest ever acquisition.

ABB chief executive officer Morten Wierod has streamlined its portfolio since taking over nearly two years ago to tap into burgeoning investment in the data centres underpinning the AI boom. The Zurich-based manufacturer last year sold its robotics division for more than US$5 billion and focused on targeted acquisitions.

title: Singapore's Sea starts enterprise cloud foray while eyeing fintech arm IPO
article:
(Oct 20): Singapore internet giant Sea Ltd is starting a new cloud business and weighing a public listing of its financial technology (fintech) arm, seeking to bolster growth and revive a plunging stock.

The company plans to offer cloud services to businesses around the world, under a new arm called Sea Cloud, chief executive officer Forrest Li wrote in a memo to staff seen by Bloomberg News.

That shift — which would mean competing directly with the likes of Amazon Web Services and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd’s cloud operations — comes as the company is also considering spinning out and listing its financial services arm Monee, according to the memo.

“Monee is approaching the point where it can stand on its own two feet and begin its own race. Going public could give it the resources and the room to go further and faster than it can today,” Li wrote, commemorating the ninth anniversary of Sea’s stock-market debut.

The e-commerce and entertainment group is locked in a fierce battle against deep-pocketed challengers including ByteDance Ltd’s TikTok Shop and Alibaba’s Lazada. That’s as Shein and PDD Holdings Inc’s Temu are also looking to break into Southeast Asia, an emerging region of 675 million people where more shoppers are coming online. The competitive landscape is weighing on Sea’s shares, which are down more than 30% this year.

See also: Fintech GCash owner gains in debut after record Philippine IPO

A new battleground for Sea’s next stage of growth is also forming an ocean away from its home turf — in Brazil — as the Singaporean company looks to expand its Shopee online empire.

Li, who is fond of penning memos to Sea’s 80,000-plus employees, last year pledged to double down on artificial intelligence (AI), betting that this would help the company hit a trillion-dollar market capitalisation. So far, Sea has integrated AI into its daily operations, launched new AI applications and partnered with frontier labs like OpenAI in e-commerce.

The company spent two years rebuilding its in-house cloud platform to host a wave of AI applications that it can offer to other enterprises, Li said.

See also: JPMorgan and Alibaba are said among investors in Dongshan’s listing — Bloomberg

“When we built Shopee at the start of the mobile internet era, we made it mobile-first while much of our competition was still thinking in terms of websites,” said Li. “We believe AI is that moment again.”

title: Japan’s 20-year bond sale sees strongest demand on record
article:
(Oct 20): Japan’s 20-year government bond auction Tuesday saw the strongest demand on record as elevated yields underpinned buying.

The bid-to-cover ratio was 5.84, compared with 4.01 at the previous sale, and a 12-month average of 3.73. In another sign of robust investor interest, the tail, or gap between average and lowest-accepted prices, was 0.07, compared with 0.15 last month.

Japan’s super-long yields have recently approached multi-decade highs, as a global bond selloff driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East and higher oil prices added to inflation and fiscal concerns. Earlier this month, the 20-year JGB yield climbed to levels last seen three decades ago, while the 30-year yield reached a record high.

The rise in yields reflects persistent concerns over Japan’s fiscal outlook, as investors are focused on how Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will fund her planned sales-tax cut on food and soft drinks without further straining the nation’s finances. Takaichi has sought to ease market concerns, saying her administration aims to build a strong economy and achieve fiscal sustainability, while pledging to appropriately manage JGB issuance in next fiscal year’s budget.

Against that backdrop, investors are watching whether elevated yields will draw demand from domestic institutional buyers. Fukoku Mutual Life Insurance Co, the first life insurer to outline its plans for the fiscal second half, said it sees scope to move a bit more from foreign bonds into yen bonds as yields have risen more than expected.

See also: Takaichi reaffirms no deficit bonds to fund food sales tax cut

A major test for Japanese bonds will come at the Bank of Japan’s policy meeting next week. While markets widely expect the central bank to keep rates unchanged, with overnight index swaps pricing in about a 6.2% chance of a hike, traders will look to governor Kazuo Ueda’s post-decision press conference for signals on the pace and scope for further tightening.

title: Australia to sue Facebook, TikTok for alleged breaches of ban
article:
(Oct 20): Australia’s government is set to sue Facebook, TikTok and other major digital platforms for alleged non-compliance with a nationwide social media ban for under-16s, Communications Minister Anika Wells said in an interview.

The country’s online safety regulator, eSafety Commissioner, said in March it was investigating Facebook and Instagram — both owned by Meta Platforms Inc — TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube for potentially failing to adhere to the law. The legislation requires the companies to take reasonable steps to stop underage users from holding social media accounts, part of a bid to protect them from harmful online content.

In an interview in Sydney on Monday, Wells said she expected legal action to proceed against the five platforms.

An eSafety report in July found most underage social media users were able to keep their accounts or create new ones, largely due to a lack of effective age checks on the platforms.

Since Australia’s world-first ban came into force almost a year ago, the government has doubled the maximum penalty for breaches to A$109.2 million (US$76 million). The government also granted eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant greater investigative powers, including the ability to demand documents from social media platforms and summon current or ex-employees to answer questions.

“Now she has more powers to be able to gather the evidence that she needs to take those five companies to the Federal Court,” Wells said. “She’s now using those powers to prepare her case.”Spokespersons for Meta and eSafety had no immediate comments. Representatives for Snapchat owner Snap Inc, TikTok and its owner ByteDance Ltd, and YouTube parent Google didn’t immediately reply to emails seeking responses to the minister’s comments.

See also: Data centre firm Elice plunges 33% in debut sunk by AI worry

The eSafety Commissioner is an independent regulator, though part of the government and accountable to Australia’s parliament through the communications minister, a position currently held by Wells. Last week, Wells said companies aren’t doing enough to adhere to social media age restrictions.

“The law is not failing — platforms are failing to comply with the law,” Wells said in an Oct 15 speech to the National Press Club. “We won’t flinch at holding tech companies to account.”

title: Nscale, Anthropic in talks for US$45 bil cloud computing deal — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 20): Nscale Ltd, the artificial intelligence (AI) cloud computing firm, is in talks to sell computing power to Anthropic PBC in a deal that could be worth about US$45 billion ($57.5 billion), according to people familiar with the negotiations.

The Nvidia Corp-backed data centre developer is seeking a second major deal with the firm behind Claude for a second facility at its Monarch data centre campus in West Virginia, the people said. Anthropic has agreements in place with Nscale for infrastructure that’s worth as much as about US$44.6 billion, according to a regulatory filing for Nscale’s planned initial public offering (IPO).

The second Monarch building would deliver 460 megawatts of computing power, using Nvidia’s advanced Vera Rubin AI chips, some of the people said. Anthropic also has the right of first refusal on Monarch’s expected third building, they said.

A deal could be finalised as soon as in the coming days, the people said, asking not to be identified as the discussions are private. Deliberations are ongoing, details of the plan could change and no final decisions have been made, the people said. Representatives of Anthropic and Nscale declined to comment.

Another multibillion-dollar computing deal would bolster Nscale’s IPO prospects as it seeks about a US$30 billion valuation in its market debut. A cohort of investors urged the firm to lower its IPO valuation target, Bloomberg News has reported.

Anthropic, which is one of Nscale’s biggest customers, has emerged as a major client for data centre providers in general. Deals it has inked include a US$50 billion pact with Fluidstack Ltd, US$10 billion with infrastructure start-up Volta Infrastructure Holdings Ltd and US$45 billion with Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

See also: AEM’s Kabbani stresses company’s tech chops to ride on AI-driven semi-con wave

Nscale’s Monarch campus in West Virginia is scalable to more than eight gigawatts of gross power when complete, the IPO filing documents showed.

Part of the Monarch campus was initially expected to be leased by Microsoft Corp, which had announced in March it signed a letter of intent for the planned data centre. But Microsoft walked away from the West Virginia site in the summer, allowing Anthropic to become the tenant, Bloomberg News reported.

Anthropic, which was valued at US$965 billion in May, is expected to conduct its own potentially record-breaking IPO in the coming months, and continues to hunt for more computing power to keep growing.

See also: The AI industry isn’t ready for the coming AI catastrophe

Investors have grown increasingly wary of the vast sums being borrowed to finance the AI data centre boom, souring on everything from chipmakers’ stocks to the debt of cloud-computing firms.

Nscale filed publicly for a US listing in September, and has yet to begin formal marketing even though the required 15 day waiting period has elapsed. The company is working through comments from the US Securities and Exchange Commission on its filing, and intends to kick off marketing when those are resolved, people familiar with the matter have said.

The company raised US$3.36 billion in a pre-IPO financing round last month in a deal led by Dan Loeb’s Third Point with investors including Nvidia, Apollo Global Management Inc, Citadel, Hudson Bay Capital and Abu Dhabi Investment Council participating.

title: Asian LNG prices jump to highest since 2022 on tanker strikes
article:
(Oct 20): Asian liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices rose to the highest in almost four years, as attacks on tankers in the Middle East damped hopes for a recovery in exports from the war-torn region.

Spot prices jumped to US$30.4 per million British thermal units on Monday, according to traders, the highest since December 2022. The UK Maritime Trade Operations received a report over the weekend that an LNG carrier was fired on near Yemen on Saturday, part of a recent increase in strikes on oil and gas vessels in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz.

The US-Iran war has trapped most Qatari LNG production, which used to account for about a fifth of global supply, behind Hormuz, forcing buyers to turn to the more expensive spot market as they can’t get enough contracted deliveries. That’s coinciding with an increase in demand as the Northern Hemisphere winter approaches, pushing prices to three times the level they were at before the conflict started in late February.

Some Asian buyers are continuing to buy spot shipments at the high price levels, intensifying competition for the super-chilled fuel with Europe. Gas-storage levels there are at 75% full, compared with a five-year seasonal average of 89%.

The energy crunch is boosting household power bills and inflation, while forcing some economies to rely more heavily on coal. South Korea’s energy minister said last week that the country would lean on the dirtiest fossil fuel and nuclear power to cope with a jump in electricity demand over winter.

See also: Qatar LNG cargo makes rare Red Sea journey to get gas to Europe

title: Takaichi reaffirms no deficit bonds to fund food sales tax cut
article:
(Oct 20): Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reiterated that she won’t rely on special deficit-covering bonds to fund a sales tax cut on food after her earlier remarks sparked speculation that she was changing her stance.

In a post on X late Monday, Takaichi wrote that she isn’t ruling out issuing government bonds to fund the national budget as a whole but she won’t rely on special deficit-covering bonds to cover a shortfall in income from the temporary sales tax cut.

The government’s position “remains unchanged,” she wrote. Takaichi said she was clarifying her position after some media reports appeared to misrepresent remarks she made earlier Monday in parliament.

At a budget committee meeting of the upper house, Takaichi said she wouldn’t rule out issuing government bonds when asked about how the sales tax cut would be funded.

“Regarding funding for the consumption tax rate reduction on food and beverages, within the broader framework of budget formulation reform, we will carefully examine the fiscal scale that would also enable us to reduce the debt-to-GDP ratio while closely monitoring tax revenue trends and proceeding with a review of both expenditures and revenues,” Takaichi said.

“We will appropriately control the total annual issuance of government bonds through both the initial budget and supplementary budgets, just as we did last fiscal year. This does not mean we are ruling out the issuance of government bonds,” she said.

The market has been paying close attention to how Takaichi would fund the sales tax cut, which is expected to cost ¥5 trillion (US$31.5 billion) per year, without further straining the nation’s debt burden. The temporary tax cut is expected to start in April and last for two years.

title: JPMorgan wealth advisers create firm overseeing US$18.6 bil
article:
(Oct 20): Two former JPMorgan Chase & Co wealth management partners have left the bank to launch their own firm managing US$18.6 billion in client assets, instantly making it one of the country’s biggest registered investment advisers.

Jim Atwood and Phil Scott announced Monday the creation of Latigo Peak Partners, a Palm Beach Gardens, Florida-based wealth advisory firm with 48 employees. The firm’s initial assets make it one of the largest “breakaway” deals in recent years, where advisers start a new firm and take many of their clients with them.

“There are not a lot of things out there where you get better as you get older. We’ve been doing this for 40 years, and plan on going for another 20 years,” Atwood said in an interview. “We want to build a family legacy business.”

Major employers have been taking notice of the trend: UBS Group AG recently increased compensation for thousands of its wealth advisers in the US after a series of high-profile exits from the firm. Last year, two other ex-JPMorgan bankers launched their own firm, Alta Vera Global Capital Advisors, managing US$400 million in assets.

Atwood, 65, and Scott, 71, both began their careers at Merrill Lynch and later joined First Republic, which was acquired by JPMorgan in 2023. They most recently worked alongside each other managing JPMorgan’s wealth units in Boston and Bellevue, Washington, respectively. That depth of experience helped convince them that starting their own firm would give them more flexibility in managing their clients’ assets.

See also: Morgan Stanley enters UK savings market with Raisin partnership

“If you’re working within one of these firms, you’re confined to investment opportunities on their platform,” Atwood said. “It gets difficult to be as nimble as you want.”

Latigo Peak will focus on public equity investing, and also offer a suite of services more typically associated with a multifamily office, including tax planning, estate planning and advice on philanthropic giving. The firm’s creation was first reported by Barron’s.

See also: PHP agrees £700 mil UK private hospital venture with GIC

The business is backed entirely by the partners’ own capital, bucking a yearslong trend of independent RIAs seeking outside financing to scale up their operations. Much of that money has come from PE: private equity backed 88% of all deals in the RIA industry last year, according to a Fidelity Investments report.

“If you look at at the top 25 RIAs, there are only one or two that are not PE-backed,” Atwood said. “We had a lot of opportunities out there to partner with PE — but when you partner with another firm, what comes with that is they’re going to want to get out in five or six years. They’re going to have an idea of how to manage the business.”

“Phil and I are backing this 100% ourselves, which is a big differentiator,” he added. “It’s not cheap to do that.”

Scott and Atwood said they generated combined revenue at JPMorgan of more than US$130 million, a nearly fourfold increase from six years prior. The plan is to keep growing: Atwood estimated that more than 95% of the firm’s new business is coming from word-of-mouth referrals.

Both Atwood and Scott have homes in the Palm Beach area, and chose the location for the firm’s headquarters in part because of the growing demand they saw for wealth management services in the region.

“A lot of people are starting to have liquidity events — there wasn’t nearly as much M&A activity five years ago as there is today,” Scott said.

Latigo Peak also has offices in Bellevue, Boston and Los Angeles, and is looking at opening locations in Denver and Jackson Hole, Wyoming, within a year, Scott said.

The firm is named in part for a ski run at the Beaver Creek resort in Colorado. Atwood and Scott met at the mountain 35 years ago, where they’ve long had an annual get-together with a number of industry colleagues.

“There’s a run out of Beaver Creek called Latigo. We used to put on the helmets and see who could get down the fastest,” Atwood said.

title: Keppel REIT to acquire 51% stake in Keppel South Central for $610.9 mil; sponsor to provide five-year income support
article:
Keppel REIT is acquiring a 51% stake in Keppel South Central from its sponsor, Keppel, for $610.9 million. The agreement was negotiated at an agreed property value of $626.2 million, which translates to around $2,350 per square foot (psf) on a 70-year leasehold basis.

According to an Oct 20 bourse filing by Keppel REIT, the initial property yield will be at 4.3%, which includes guaranteed monthly income support of $2.23 million for up to five years, to be arranged by Keppel.

The manager of Keppel REIT adds that the proposed income support arrangement will be done at current rents at the property.

As at Sept 30, committed leases and leases which are in the process of documentation for Keppel South Central comprised 52.7% of net lettable area (NLA) at an average rent of approximately $11.30 psf per month, which is above the rent of S$11.15 psf per month assumed under the arrangement.

“The rent of $11.30 psf per month largely reflects leasing activity on the lower-to-mid floors, with potential for higher rents from the remaining available space on the mid-to-high floors,” says the manager of Keppel REIT.

As at Oct 15, committed leases and leases which are in the process of documentation for Keppel South Central had increased to approximately 60%.

See also: Parkway Life REIT to acquire another three nursing homes in France for €38.8 mil

The manager intends to fund the acquisition through a combination of bank loans, perpetual securities, internal cash and/or equity financing with post-acquisition aggregate leverage expected to be 39.2%.

Assuming that this proposed acquisition and the divestment of both T Tower and KR Ginza II had been completed on Jan 1, the pro forma distribution per unit (DPU) accretion will be at 2.01%.

“With an acquisition structure that provides income stability and potential future upside, the transaction positions us well to deliver sustainable long-term returns for our unitholders,” says Chua Hsien Yang, CEO of the manager of Keppel REIT.

See also: Starhill Global REIT divests Ebisu Fort for JPY6.2 bil, 53.8% above valuation

Completion of this proposed acquisition is subject to the approval of unitholders at an extraordinary general meeting, which is expected to be held in 4Q2026 and this transaction is expected to be completed in 2Q2027.

Units in Keppel REIT closed unchanged at 82.5 cents on Oct 19, while shares of Keppel Limited closed 3 cents lower, or down 0.3%, at $10.07.

title: US stock futures edge higher after chipmaker rally
article:
(Oct 20) : US stock futures edged higher in early Tuesday trading, extending a rebound sparked by chipmakers that helped the Nasdaq 100 recover from its worst week since the tariff turmoil of April 2025.

Nasdaq 100 contracts rose 0.2% after the underlying gauge gained 1.2% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index climbed 1.6%, snapping an eight-day losing streak. S&P 500 futures added 0.1%. The rebound looked less convincing for Asian stocks, with contracts for Japan, South Korea and Australia all pointing lower. Hong Kong traders were set to return from a holiday.

The durability of any equity rebound will be tested this week after concerns over AI spending and higher interest rates rattled markets. Earnings from Meta Platforms Inc. and Tesla Inc. will offer clues on whether profit growth can sustain elevated valuations and investment, while Nscale Ltd. was said to be in talks on a US$45 billion computing deal with Anthropic PBC.

Oil remained elevated near multi-month highs, adding to pressure on bonds. The 10-year Treasury yield rose seven basis points to 5.14% on Monday as the recovery in technology shares reduced haven demand and traders rebuilt wagers on Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes next year. French bonds also came under pressure following violent unrest over the weekend.

“Results will show whether strong profit growth can restore confidence in the equity rally,” said Mark Haefele at UBS Chief Investment Office. “We continue to expect resilient growth and earnings to support equities, and see attractive opportunities in quality bonds.”

CoreWeave Inc., a bellwether for the AI infrastructure trade, fell 0.4% even after Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to buy, citing its revenue potential and tight computing capacity. The shares plunged last week as the company’s debt dropped to levels typically associated with distress, adding to concerns about the durability of the AI boom.

See also: Oil wavers as Iran threats vie with robust Gulf crude flows

Elsewhere in Asia, China’s central bank signalled its overnight reverse repurchase rate will replace the current seven-day rate as its policy benchmark, another step toward aligning its framework with global peers that may help lower borrowing costs.

Oil fluctuated as technical resistance tempered gains driven by renewed supply risks from the Middle East conflict. Brent settled above $109 a barrel after jumping almost 4% Friday as traders positioned for the risk of an escalation in the Iran war.

Prices briefly rose Monday before easing after Iran said it had “no choice” but to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz, while US lawmakers continued to resist President Donald Trump’s diesel export deal with Russia.

See also: Nasdaq 100 climbs on AI trade revival after rout

Treasury yields climbed six to eight basis points across maturities as the rebound in equities reduced haven buying and traders rebuilt bets on Fed tightening next year. Markets continued to price another quarter-point increase in December.

“Market positioning is still quite tenuous given the recent whipsaw selloff and rally, which is keeping a lot of investors away, exacerbating the day-to-day moves,” said Gennadiy Goldberg, head of US interest rates strategy at TD Securities.

title: Oil wavers as Iran threats vie with robust Gulf crude flows
article:
(Oct 20) : Oil wavered as traders weighed the prospect of an escalation in hostilities by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz against robust crude flows from the Persian Gulf.

The most-active West Texas Intermediate contract traded around US$98 a barrel after swinging in a range of about US$3 in the previous session. Brent settled at US$109.55, near a five-month high. Iran has “no choice” but to assert control over Hormuz to safeguard the country’s security, First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said Monday, state-run news agency IRNA reported.

Despite the recent flareup in hostilities around the waterway, crude exports from the Gulf have continued at an accelerated pace. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Fox News that flows had recovered to about 80% of their prewar level, although refined-product shipments remained constrained.

Brent has surged about 80% this year as widening conflicts in the Middle East and between Russia and Ukraine disrupt energy supplies. Refined products have rallied even harder, with European diesel futures surging. Still, while Persian Gulf crude flows are recovering, renewed attacks on tankers and energy infrastructure are keeping the outlook fragile and geopolitical risk elevated.

Meanwhile, the Trump administration is authorizing the sale of sanctioned oil tankers to allow them to ship crude, according to Wright. He estimated that there are about 1,600 vessels in the global “dark fleet.”

title: Nasdaq 100 climbs on AI trade revival after rout
article:
(Oct 20) : A rebound in chipmakers buoyed the stock market as dip buyers emerged on bets the artificial-intelligence investment boom will continue to support solid earnings.

Following a rout in one of the most-crowded bets, a gauge of chip giants climbed 1.6%. The Nasdaq 100 added 1.2%. Nscale Ltd. was said to be in talks to sell computing power to Anthropic PBC in a deal that could be worth about US$45 billion. This week’s earnings from Meta Platforms Inc. will provide a fresh test for confidence in the AI trade. Tesla Inc. is also due to report.

Oil prices remained at elevated levels, weighing on Treasuries. The market also came under pressure as French bonds got hit after a weekend of violent unrest.

The advance in tech stocks lost steam last week as investors questioned the sustainability of AI spending, given the outlook for higher rates. The industry is still set to account for nearly 70% of global earnings growth next year, according to Citigroup Inc.

“Results will show whether strong profit growth can restore confidence in the equity rally,” said Mark Haefele at UBS Chief Investment Office. “We continue to expect resilient growth and earnings to support equities, and see attractive opportunities in quality bonds.”

While the recent semiconductor selloff was jarring, Lisa Shalett at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management saw the market action as healthy. The reason is that it has recalibrated yields and awakened corners of the market from complacency.

See also: Brent crude holds near US$110 on Mideast and Ukraine conflicts

“That said, growth and earnings remain strong, equity valuations have improved and the AI-capex cycle — dominated by rate-insensitive hyperscalers — is secure,” she added. “2027 should feature slowing capex growth, cooling inflation comparisons and further valuation reversion toward sustainable trend profit growth.”

The final three months of the year have historically been favorable for stocks. Although there is no guarantee these historical patterns will continue in 2026, strong corporate profit growth and resilient economic activity could support further gains through year-end, according to Brock Weimer at Edward Jones.

At Morgan Stanley, Michael Wilson says investors should prepare to add risk to their portfolios as a months-long pullback in parts of the equity market nears an end.

See also: US stock futures rise ahead of busy earnings week

“We advise investors to be ready for either a very rapid reconciliation or a slower bleed into November because in our view, that will be the time to add risk rather than shun it,” he noted.

title: Digital gold market worth US$700 bil
article:
A survey has revealed that nearly nine in ten retail investors are open to investing in digital gold under the “right” conditions, suggesting latent demand with an estimated market value of US$700 ($896) billion. If fully-realised, this broadly matches the market for physically backed gold ETFs.

Conducted by the World Gold Council (WGC) and Boston Consulting Group (BCG), the study, entitled Digital Gold: Unlocking a US$700bn Opportunity, provides a five-year base case which sees digital gold growing by around 27% annually to US$160-170 billion by 2031. A bull case would see the market grow to US$270-280 billion by 2031.

The digital gold market is currently estimated to be worth US$45-55 billion, with tokenised gold, one segment of the digital gold market alongside vaulted digital gold, growing fivefold in value since late 2024 to around US$6 billion. With cumulative spot trading volumes in tokenised gold reaching around US$90 billion in 1Q2026 (according to CoinGecko), the report suggests that the digital gold market could be at an inflection point.

“Significant investor interest in digital gold is clear, but demand cannot scale without the right infrastructure behind it,” says WGC CEO David Tait.

The most significant barrier to investing in digital gold is trust according to investors. Stronger consumer protections, transparent proof of backing, accessible redemption and clearer regulation are cited by investors to be the important factors in influencing their confidence in digital gold.

“Trust has always been the biggest and most important factor for gold products,” says Robin Kolvenbach, CEO of Swiss precious metals refinery Argor-Heraeus.

See also: Gold steady as Fed official’s remarks temper rate-hike bets

Reported by The Edge Singapore earlier, Singapore Bullion Market Association CEO Albert Cheng says that the industry must be “extra careful” and ensure that the investor understands what is being sold when allowing retail participation in digital gold products. “A higher level of disclosure is required,” he said. “Clarity on fees, investor understanding, proper safeguards and product credibility are essential.”

Cheng added that the physical gold must remain the foundation of digital gold, saying, “You must have a very clear governance structure and legal framework to tie in the tokenised product to the physical layer.”

To this end, the WGC has been developing Gold as a Service (GaaS), a shared infrastructure that provides gold token product developers with an operating layer or “digitally native layer” of physical gold. Through GaaS, WGC aims to enhance the fungibility of gold tokens, turning fragmented digital gold products into a single investable category and enabling tokenised gold to function as a financial asset.

See also: Gold steadies as traders assess US-Iran tensions, Fed rate path

"Building a liquid, trusted market will require the wider industry to work to the same standards, so investors can have confidence in what they are buying,” adds Tait.

The report also pointed out that access to digital gold as another barrier to higher adoption, suggesting that payment and banking apps, in markets such as China, India and Indonesia, are central to market penetration. This is due to consumer familiarity and trust in these platforms.

In addition, while physical gold and gold-backed ETFs are unable to provide yield, gold tokens could overcome this constraint and make gold investing more attractive. “If gold yields on tokenised gold are moving in tandem with US Treasury yields, then the adverse case for holding gold is substantially undermined,” says Daragh Maher, head of digital assets research at HSBC.

Solving the afore-mentioned barriers and costs issues could expand the gold market, rather than just redistribute demand, with around 65% of the latent demand sitting with people who do not yet own gold, suggests the report.

“We undertook this project with the belief that gold has the potential to become the world’s most credible digital asset - not despite its physical nature, but because of it,” says Urs Rahne, managing director and partner of BCG. “Our research has reinforced our confidence in the scale of this opportunity and provided a clearer understanding of what it will take to realise its full potential.”

Among today’s digital gold investors, 52% held no gold before their first digital purchase, of which 92% have since bought other forms of gold, highlighting the report’s finding that digital gold can act as an entry point to the wider gold market. Younger investors are leading the way, with awareness of digital gold reaching 50% among 25–34-year-olds, compared with 23% among those aged 55 and over.
